 Coram:
 Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra
Order Order
01. 1. Heard.

2. At the instance of the opposite party no.2, the F.I.R., i.e., Raghunathpur P.S. Case No.84 of 2024 came to be registered against the petitioner under Sections 376(1)/506 of the I.P.C. read with Sections 67 & 67A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C.-cum- Grama Nyayalaya, Raghunathpur.

3. In the F.I.R., it is alleged that the opposite party no.2 was taking apprenticeship training at Gruha and Purta Bibhaga (R & B) Section, Jajpur, the Junior Engineer, Binaya Kumar Sahoo, the present petitioner took her to Puri in his car and stayed in an unknown hotel.
While staying in the hotel, the petitioner committed rape on her by threatening.
The petitioner took some photos and videos in his mobile phone during intimacy.
The petitioner forced her to keep physical relationship by showing those photographs and video clippings.

4. The petitioner and opposite party no.2 present in Court today along with their respective counsel and they have filed their self attested photocopies of Adhar Cards to establish their identity, which are taken on record.
5.

The petitioner and opposite party no.2 have filed a joint affidavit dated 08.05.2024 inter alia stating that they have settled their dispute by intervention of local Sarpanch and family members in the temple of Gorekhnath.
They have decided put quietus to the dispute and lead peaceful life separately and further decided to destroy all the photographs and video clippings.
The said affidavit is a part of the records.

The terms of settlement dated 13.04.2024 has been produced before the I.O.
under Annexure-2.

1 are taken on record.
The petitioner in his affidavit inter alia
stated that they shall remain separate to lead peaceful life leaving all kind of relationship.
He further stated that he has deleted the joint photos and video clippings.
The pen drive, which was in his possession, has been handed over to the Opposite party before this Court.
The opposite party no.2 has received the pen drive in Court today.

Therefore, in view of the settlement, the petitioner seeks indulgence of this Court by quashing the F.I.R.
6.
Mr. Maharaj, learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State submits that investigation is still going on.

During investigation, the parties have submitted the terms of settlement before the I.O.
which has been taken note of.
Although charge sheet has not been filed, however, parties have settled their dispute.

Therefore, there is no legal impediment to quash the F.I.R.
7.
The petitioner has handed over the pen drive which was in his possession to the opposite party no.2 in Court today and opposite party no.2 has taken the pen drive.
8. Taking into consideration the aforementioned facts the opposite party no.2 is not willing to proceed against the petitioner.

Therefore, the present petition is squarely covered by the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303 and B.S. Joshi & others vs. State of Haryana & another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675

9. Taking into consideration the aforementioned judgments, facts of the case and submission made at bar, Raghunathpur P.S. Case No.84 of 2024 corresponding to G.R. Case No.81 of 2024 pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C. -cum - Grama Nyayalaya, Raghunathpur and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom qua the petitioner are quashed.
9. The petitioner is directed to pay Rs.10,000/- to the opposite party no.2 in Court today on receipt of which she will file the receipt thereof.
10. The CRLMC is accordingly disposed of.
